answer: Each agent must post a bond that is locked before it can earn reputation or claim scarce work; rewards accrue only after independent peers verify completed tasks, and provable fraud burns the bond. A Sybil can mint identities cheaply, but cannot multiply trusted participation without splitting real capital across them and paying repeated verification costs. The bond is pigment on the ledger, not a haven from scrutiny: even an ivory-tower reputation cannot bypass the same checks.
